text:
Sam: Noticed a trend: invoice_preview showing higher token totals than final invoices for tenants in preview buckets. Roughly +15% on average. Saw it starting at ~2026-03-19 02:00 UTC.

Priya: Is this related to the preview sampling pipeline or the aggregator dedupe window?

Sam: My hunch is aggregator dedupe key collision when fallback routing to smaller models occurs during canary. We tag preview requests with sampling_id, but fallback path sometimes rewrites sampling_id -> null. If aggregator drops into 'no-key' bucket we might double-count across windows.

Luis: Can you show an example event chain?

Sam: Pasted sequence: edge emitted request event -> routing fallback to small-quant -> aggregator emitted two partial aggregates (one with sampling_id, one without) -> invoice_preview picked the union.

Ivy: That would inflate preview because preview uses pre-aggregation snapshotted counts. Final billing replays raw events with strict dedupe on req_id so it collapses to single.

Sam: exact example: request_id=rid-20260319-9001
```
edge: {"req_id":"rid-20260319-9001","tenant":"globex","sampling_id":"smp-81","model_requested":"gpt4-large","route":"preview-canary"}
router: fallback to model_served=gpt4-small-quant, sampling_id rewritten -> null
aggregator: emit partial agg for sampling_id=smp-81 tokens=450
aggregator: emit partial agg for sampling_id=null tokens=50
invoice_preview: merged partials -> tokens_preview=500
final_billing: raw events dedup by req_id -> tokens_final=450
```

Priya: So preview used sampling_id + null bucket union. That makes sense. Why is sampling_id getting nulled on fallback? That's new. Any recent router changes?

deploy-bot: Deployed service router v2.4.0 at 2026-03-18T23:45Z by ci/pipeline. Changes: normalize model_alias on fallback; also added fallback-path rewriting to keep vendor postfix removal.

Luis: Which explains it. Normalization code path likely forgot to carry sampling_id through rewrite.

Ivy: Short-term: we can change invoice_preview to prefer req_id dedupe over sampling_id union when req_id present. Long-term: fix router to preserve sampling_id.

Sam: Agreed. For immediate mitigation, can we run a targeted preview re-merge that drops null sampling bucket for preview window 2026-03-18T22:00..2026-03-19T04:00 for tenants in preview groups? We need to avoid touching live final billing.

Priya: Also add a dashboard panel: preview_vs_final_tokens (%) by tenant with alert when delta > 5% for 30m. That will catch regressions in future rollouts.

Luis: I'll open PR to router to carry sampling_id on fallback and add unit test. Also adding schema contract test between router and aggregator: sampling_id must be present or explicit "sampling_id_null_reason" set.

Sam: I'll prepare a list of affected tenants by querying preview aggregates where sampling_id is null AND exists matching raw req_id in raw.events.

Sam: query I ran:
```
SELECT tenant_id, req_id, SUM(tokens) as preview_tokens
FROM preview.aggregates
WHERE window_start >= '2026-03-18T22:00:00Z' AND window_end <= '2026-03-19T04:00:00Z'
  AND sampling_id IS NULL
GROUP BY tenant_id, req_id
HAVING SUM(tokens) > 0
LIMIT 200;
```

Sam: got ~42 tenants, attaching CSV to BILL-3388.

billing-bot: BILL-3388 created: "preview/final delta investigation" assigned to @Ivy. Link: https://billing.redwood/tickets/BILL-3388

Ivy: For reconciliation: we can either backfill previews for affected tenants (recompute preview aggregates using req_id dedupe), or mark those preview entries as "ignored" for invoice_preview metric aggregation. Which is less risky?

Priya: Recomputing previews is safer; ignoring data hides the issue. But recompute cost might be heavy.

Sam: We can recompute only for affected tenant windows (CSV list) — write a one-off job that replays raw events into preview_agg with req_id-first dedupe key. I have a helper script.

Luis: Timeline: PR to router + tests -> revert v2.4.0 normalization in canary OR patch to preserve sampling_id. Deploy hotfix to canary tonight. Recompute previews over next 24h. Add dashboard/alert.

Ivy: I'll coordinate with billing ops for any invoice_preview adjustments and notify affected customers if the recompute changes invoice estimates.

Priya: Postmortem action items: (1) schema contract (router->aggregator), (2) preview_vs_final delta alert, (3) add dedupe precedence docs in metering runbook, (4) test harness that simulates fallback rewriting.

Sam: OK. I'll queue the recompute job and attach logs to BILL-3388. Thanks all.

Luis: TY. Follow-up: can we add a small e2e test in canary that sends synthetic req with sampling_id and forces fallback? That would have prevented this.

Priya: yes I'll add that to the rollout checklist in Console UX for preview experiments.

Sam: updating ticket with CSV + job plan now."
